name: Advanced Micro Devices
thesis: Data Center growth, four straight beats and fast-rising estimates argue for the shares; valuation and weak free cash flow argue against. The evidence tilts higher, but not strongly enough for a directional view.

note.name: Advanced Micro Devices
note.thesis: Data Center growth, four straight beats and fast-rising estimates argue for the shares; valuation and weak free cash flow argue against. The evidence tilts higher, but not strongly enough for a directional view.
note.what: AMD designs high-performance processors and accelerators and sells them fabless, mostly made by TSMC. Data Center sells EPYC server CPUs and Instinct GPUs to hyperscalers and cloud builders; Client and Gaming sells Ryzen PC chips and console semi-custom parts; Embedded serves industrial and communications customers.

points.text: Q3 revenue $13.38B topped guidance's high end, up 44.7% y/y. Non-GAAP EPS $2.09 beat the $1.95 consensus; GAAP EPS $1.46 included a $1.1B non-cash warrant charge.
Data Center revenue was $8.5B, up 97% y/y and 64% of total against 47% a year earlier. Helios rackscale runs at Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle.
Next-fiscal-year EPS consensus rose to $17.69 from $15.78 in 30 days, with 10 revisions up and 1 down. The last four quarters each beat.
Q3 free cash flow fell to $554M from $1.56B, while inventory rose about $3B to $11.5B to support 2027 capacity.
The counterweight is valuation: the forward multiple is close to double the peer median and the price assumes the full 2027 plan, leaving little room for a slip.

note.supplyHeadline: Mild dilution, net cash, deals add shares
note.supplyText: Diluted shares went from 1.64B to 1.66B over the year, up 1.2%, and management guides the fourth quarter to about 1.67B including the Taalas and World Labs acquisitions. On the company's basis cash and short-term investments of $15.8B exceed debt of $7.1B; Yahoo's trailing figures are $15.78B cash and $9.21B debt. No dividend is paid.
note.valuationHeadline: Multiple near double the peer median
note.valuationText: Forward P/E is 33.1× on fiscal-2027 consensus EPS of $17.69, and 72.5× on this fiscal year's $8.08; the peer median is 17.7×. EV/revenue is 19.8× against a 6.2× peer median. At the median multiple, $17.69 gives $313.22 a share, 46.6% below the price — arithmetic on consensus, not a forecast.
note.usageText: Management guides fourth-quarter revenue to about $17B, plus or minus 3%, up 66% y/y, with non-GAAP gross margin near 55%, Data Center up roughly 50% q/q and Client and Gaming down more than 20%. Revenue dipped slightly in the March 2026 quarter before the June and September rises.

catalysts.text: Q4 results; consensus EPS $2.93, revenue $17.06B, beyond this window

risks.title: Revisions reverse
risks.text: Next-fiscal-year EPS revisions turn net negative, removing the support the multiple relies on.

risks.title: Data Center slows
risks.text: Fourth-quarter Data Center growth lands below management's roughly 50% q/q, or the 2027 doubling is cut.

risks.title: Margin erosion
risks.text: Gross margin guidance near 55% gives way as memory and component costs rise.

risks.title: Weak cash conversion
risks.text: Free cash flow stays near Q3's $554M while inventory keeps building.

Q4 2026: Taalas and World Labs acquisitions guided to close

note.positioningText: Short interest is 38.6M shares, 2.4% of the float and 1.91 days of volume to cover, down from 39.3M a month earlier. The at-the-money straddle expiring 19 Feb 2027 prices a ±25.4% move. Estimate revisions run net positive.
note.conclusion: Estimates and delivery support the growth story; the multiple against peers and weak free cash flow argue the other way. Data Center is close to the whole business, so its execution carries the note. The next firm evidence is the 2 February report, which sits beyond the eight-week window.
note.invalidation: Next-fiscal-year EPS revisions turn net negative for 30 days, or Q4 Data Center growth misses guidance.
note.gaps: No buyback authorization or repurchase amounts appeared in the material read, no insider sale transactions are dated, and no analyst targets newer than the 12 November aggregate. Export-rule and tariff outcomes are undated, so the regulatory risk cannot be timed.
